title: Surge containment simulation and graceful tenant ejection
creator: Priya Rao
description: Summary: After the 2026-02-08 hosted API capacity event we observed persistent queue buildup on multiple GPU pools driven by a set of mid-tail tenant bursts combined with autoscaler hysteresis and KV cache pollution. This ticket captures the follow-ups: build a tenant-aware surge simulator, prototype a 'capacity corral' containment primitive, and implement a graceful tenant ejection/pacing mechanism with new telemetry and a runbook for on-call. The goal is to reduce rescue escalations and enable deterministic containment within SLOs for future multi-tenant storms.
timeline: 2026-02-08 03:12 UTC - alert: pool latency SLO breach; downstream queues rising. 03:19 UTC - on-call applied emergency soft-throttle for top 5 noisy tenants. 03:45 UTC - attempted rolling scale-up hit provisioning delay; queues remained elevated. 06:00 UTC - KV cache hit-rate dropped across bursty tenants, increasing per-token work. 09:20 UTC - incident declared stable; mitigation included tenant throttles and routing of low-priority traffic to cold fallback models. Post-incident analysis showed correlated mid-tail bursts plus autoscaler hysteresis causing prolonged queue persistence.
root_cause: 1) Autoscaler hysteresis and conservative scale step sizing allowed demand to overshoot before capacity matched, leading to queue amplification. 2) Tenant KV cache pollution: a few tenants' requests used wide-context prompts that flushed shared prefix cache and elevated token compute. 3) Lack of a containment primitive: we had no targeted ejection/pacing policy that could quickly remove a small set of noisy tenants without global throttles. 4) Insufficient per-tenant queue SLI and early-warning signals — alerts are pool-level only.
short_term_mitigations: Deploy emergency soft-throttle Lambda: target top-10 noisy tenants by credit score; temp reduce concurrency by 30% (rollout: staged across regions)
Increase autoscaler aggressiveness window for hosted pools during verified surges (temporary config change)
Enable per-tenant KV cache isolation flag for high-noise tenants (experimental, 48h observation)
Add a dashboard: per-pool + per-tenant queue depth heatmap and 95th queue grow-rate alert
long_term_action_items: ENG-256902: Build "capacity corral" primitive — ephemeral soft-pool that isolates noisy tenant traffic and applies conservative KV cache limits
ENG-256903: Tenant-aware packing & eviction simulator (deterministic) to run replayed traffic and test ejection policies before deploy
ENG-256904: Implement eviction pacing algorithm (gradual graceful ejection over 60s window) with backoff to avoid KV cache stampede
ENG-256905: Tune autoscaler hysteresis: add probe scale-up pathway & per-tenant demand signal to avoid overshoot
ENG-256906: Expand telemetry: add SLIs 'per-tenant queue depth', 'queue grow-rate', and 'kv-cache-locality' with 1m resolution and retention 90d
ENG-256907: Create on-call runbook 'surge-corral-and-eject' with playbook steps, run frequency: once per incident, and drill schedule: quarterly
ENG-256908: Add regression tests to CI that run the packing simulator against representative traffic (nightly smoke)
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay a 24h anonymized traffic window and reproduce queue amplification cases in >90% of seeded scenarios
Capacity corral can isolate a chosen tenant set and reduce pool queue grow-rate by >=50% in synthetic tests
Eviction pacing does not cause KV cache stampede in test replays and keeps end-to-end p95 latency within SLOs during controlled ejections
New dashboard and alerts are live and actionable; first runbook drill completed and retro posted to Confluence

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive immediate ejection prevents global SLO degradation but risks client-level churn and cache stampede. We chose a paced eviction with prewarming corral as primary approach to balance client experience and platform health. Follow-ups assigned for UI/Console integration so operators can apply corrals without infra changes. Plan to coordinate with Sales/CS for tenants that may be ejected during drills.
